newsitem.title: USA: General Instrument comfortable with EPS view.
newsitem.headline: General Instrument comfortable with EPS view.

text.p: General Instrument Corp said on Wednesday it is comfortable with analysts' consensus earnings estimate of $0.20 a share for its first quarter.

General Instrument Chief Executive Richard Friedland, when asked if he was comfortable with the consensus estimate, said, "Yes. We try not to leave any misconceptions out in the market, to the extent we understand what's going on."
According to First Call, analysts expect the company to report earnings of $0.20 a share versus $0.24 last year.
General Instrument, which makes set-top cable boxes and other telecommunications products, is expected to report its first-quarter results in mid-April.
The company is in the process of restructuring into three independent companies, to be completed this summer.
For the fourth quarter, the company reported a net loss of $0.12 a share versus a profit of $0.43 a share.
